segments: ... month of the year one thousand and six hundred of the Greeks [1289 AD].
And in it, again, in this year,
the raiders of Syria gathered, about two thousand horsemen,
and they came and crossed into the territory of Sinjar and Beth 'Arbaye,
neither taking captives nor plundering, until they reached the vicinity of Fishabur, a village on the banks of the river Tigris.
And they lodged there.
And they arose in the night,
and crossed the river,
and set their faces toward Wasto, a large Nestorian village,
and attacked it at the deep dawn of Sunday, the fourteenth
of the month of Ab.
Now the inhabitants of the village thought that they were a few bandits,
and they went out to meet them.
And when they saw their great numbers, they retreated to the village;
some of them took refuge in the church and were saved,
and some of them scattered in the gardens and vineyards.
Then those wicked men took control of the village,
and spread out over seven villages around it,
and they then caused great destruction.
And they killed about five hundred people,
and took captive about a thousand souls—women, boys, and girls—
and took goods, sheep, and cattle without number.
And they turned back on that same day by the way they had come,
and went slowly and without fear,
until they reached the Khabur River,
over which there was a narrow bridge.
And there they were delayed by the weight of the plunder and the multitude of captives who were being driven with difficulty.
And thus the news reached the emir of the Mongols who was in Mosul,
and without delay they prepared, mounted, and pursued after them.
And they went and found them,
for most of them had already crossed over the bridge
and departed while laden with the plunder.
And those who had not yet crossed,
they killed them all.
And they recovered from the captivity about three hundred captives,
women, boys, and girls,
and brought them and handed them over to their masters.
And again in this same summer,
the raiders of Syria went out,
about two thousand horsemen,
to the regions of Melitene and of Hisn [Ziyad? / Claudia?].
And Karbanda, the commander-in-chief there, heard of it,
and he assembled {OCR?} his forces,
and they prepared, went, and engaged them,
and were shattered before them.
And many men of those who were with him were killed,
and of his friends and relatives, eleven {OCR?} were taken prisoner,
